title: API Contracts, Pagination & Edge Defense
summary: Write crisp interview-ready APIs with safe pagination, idempotency, and abuse controls.
body:
Spending five focused minutes on clean API contracts anchors your entire architecture diagram and signals production maturity.

## Protocol choice
- `REST` over HTTPS (`JSON`): default for public and CRUD-style client-to-gateway APIs.
- `gRPC` (`Protobuf` over HTTP/2): strong fit for low-latency internal service-to-service RPCs with strict schemas and streaming.
- `SSE` / `WebSockets`: add only when the server must push sub-second events without client polling.

## Pagination, mutations, and async jobs
- Cursor pagination: pass `limit` and an opaque `cursor` encoding `(sort_timestamp, last_id)` instead of `OFFSET`, which degrades linearly on deep pages and skips/duplicates rows under live inserts.
- Idempotent writes: accept an `Idempotency-Key` header (or client-generated `message_id`) stored with a TTL/unique constraint so mobile retries never create duplicate orders, charges, or messages.
- Long-running work: return `202 Accepted` with a `job_id` when work exceeds a couple hundred milliseconds (`code execution`, `video transcoding`, `compliance exports`).

## Security and abuse checklist
- Derive `user_id` and `tenant_id` from the verified auth token at the gateway—never trust caller-supplied body fields for ownership.
- Enforce rate limits (`429 Too Many Requests` + `Retry-After`) per API key, user, and IP.
- Sign outbound webhooks with `HMAC-SHA256(timestamp + body)`, and block private/loopback/metadata IP ranges on any server-side URL fetch (`SSRF`).
